text:
alex.w: Heads-up — customer reported big token delta between our SDK estimator and the invoice. SDK shows ~2.1k tokens per call, invoice ~6.2k. Happens on streaming completions that call a tool. Repro below, need help narrowing whether this is meter or tokenizer mismatch.

mira.k: Can you paste the exact request payload + how the SDK is estimating? streaming vs non-streaming?

alex.w: Repro (redacted):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \ 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \ 
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-neo-3.8b","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize this document..."}],"stream":true,"functions":[{"name":"search","url":"https://acme/search"}]}'

Node SDK call we ran (estimator lib):

const est = estimator.count({messages, model: 'rwd-neo-3.8b'});
console.log('est', est.totalTokens); // ~2100

The realtime logs show the runtime invoked the search function (server-side tool proxy) and then streamed back additional assistant tokens. The SDK estimator only counts the input messages + client-visible chunks.

billing-bot: Invoice run 2026-02-20 for acct ACME shows 6,215 tokens on that call id (job id xxxxx). Metering pipeline notes server-inserted assistant messages and tool payloads that are included in final metered tokens.

ops.jesse: Thanks for the repro. Two quick suspects: 1) server-side injections (system/tool/assistant messages added after the request) are not visible to the client estimator; 2) streaming reassembly differences — the estimator counts only bytes you pass locally, not ephemeral fragments or server-added prefixes.

samir: Also check KV/prefix cache rehydration. If the runtime prepends cached context at serve-time (prefix caching) that isn't in the original messages, the meter will include it. That often shows up when streaming + prefix + toolcall combine.

alex.w: How do we prove which buckets these extra ~4k tokens are from? Need to provide ACME a breakdown before EOD.

ops.jesse: Action plan:
- I'll pull the metering record for that call (job id) and export the token breakdown by role (system/user/assistant/tool).
- Mira, can you share the SDK estimator version and whether it uses the same tokenizer as server? If it's an older tokenizer binding it could undercount certain multi-byte tokens.
- Billing-team, please hold invoice adjustments until we confirm.

mira.k: SDK is v0.9.7 estimator module. It uses a local BPE variant; we recently changed whitespace normalization in runtime (May 2025) which changed counts slightly. But not usually 3-4k on a ~2k input.

billing-bot: Flag set: invoice hold = true for acct ACME.

ops.jesse: I pulled the job traces — preliminary breakdown: server counted ~800 tokens from a cached system prompt that was prepended, ~2.6k tokens from assistant content (includes tool response interpolation), and ~2.8k tokens from the tool response body (search results). The SDK estimator never saw the tool response body and didn't know about the cached system preface. That sums to ~6.2k.

samir: That matches my hunch. Two mitigation suggestions for customers while we fix tooling: 1) opt out of server-side prefixing for sensitive endpoints (config flag), 2) disable tool proxying in streaming tests so estimator and meter line up. We should document this in support KB.

alex.w: Good. Can we add an API-debug flag to return server-side token deltas in response headers so clients can reconcile?

ops.jesse: I can prototype a debug header (X-Redwood-Meter-Delta) for internal use. Longer-term product will expose a per-request metering breakdown. For now I'll export a CSV for ACME showing role/token columns.

mira.k: Also going to add a note in the SDK docs clarifying that client estimators only count client-visible input and that server-side injections/tool payloads are charged.

ops.jesse: Next steps and owners:
- ops.jesse: export breakdown CSV and post here (ETA 2h).
- mira.k: SDK docs clarification + check tokenizer parity (ETA end of day).
- billing-bot / billing team: keep invoice on hold and await CSV (ETA ack).
- alex.w: send ACME the CSV and suggested mitigations once posted.

alex.w: Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround. I'll keep the customer updated. :thumbsup:
